content_preview.title: AWS Interconnect Adds Microsoft Azure in Public Preview, Extending Its Multicloud Networking Spec to a Third Hyperscaler
content_preview.summary: AWS and Microsoft launched a public preview letting customers privately link AWS and Azure workloads at up to 100 Gbps, completing the open interconnect spec's rollout across Azure, OCI, and Google Cloud.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Amazon Web Services and Microsoft launched a public preview on August 31 that lets customers establish private, high-speed network links directly between AWS and Azure, according to the [AWS News Blog](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/aws-announces-AWS-interconnect-multicloud-microsoft-azure-preview/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (845 words) with clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis sections. Neutral, factual tone throughout; no sensationalism. Correctly frames the Azure preview as the follow-through on commitments AWS made in its April GA announcement, and accurately notes OCI has separately reached GA since then.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources fetched successfully (200 OK, no suspicious_patterns) and read from the gzipped snapshots in sources/2026-09/aws-interconnect-adds-microsoft-azure-in-public-preview-extending-its-multicloud-networking-spec-to-a-third-hyperscaler/: (1) source-0.html.gz (AWS News Blog, 'AWS announces AWS Interconnect - multicloud connectivity with Microsoft Azure in preview', posted Aug 31, 2026) — confirms the Aug 31 preview launch, the four listed regions (US East N. Virginia, US West N. California, Asia Pacific Sydney, Europe Frankfurt), Console/CLI/API provisioning, and the 'first purpose-built product of its kind' quote verbatim. However, the article's quoted line 'consistent connectivity experiences across Microsoft Azure (Preview), OCI (Generally Available), and Google Cloud (Generally Available)' attributed to this post as a direct quote does NOT match the source verbatim — the actual sentence reads 'This allows AWS to provide a consistent, simple experience to our customers on Microsoft Azure (Preview), OCI (Generally Available), and Google Cloud (Generally Available).' The parenthetical GA/Preview status labels are accurate, but the surrounding phrase is a paraphrase dressed as a direct quote. (2) source-1.html.gz (The Register, 'Microsoft and AWS build the multicloud bridge they said customers barely needed', published Tue 1 Sep 2026) — confirms 100 Gbps connection speed, the Kennedy quotes verbatim ('Customers told us they wanted a better way...' and 'With AWS Interconnect...scalability at the click of a button'), the Annamalai quote verbatim ('through a simplified experience that abstracts the underlying complexity of multicloud networking'), the regulator-irony claims about AWS's CMA statement and Microsoft's 'fairly specialized situations' statement, and 'AWS Interconnect – multicloud now covers all three major rival platforms: Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.' (3) source-2.html.gz (Microsoft Azure Blog, 'Introducing Azure Multicloud Interconnect for AWS', by Narayan Annamalai, VP and Head of Products Azure Networking Services, Aug 31) — confirms the Kennedy quote is independently carried here too, and the Annamalai 'broader interoperability across hyperscale cloud providers' language. Note: this source states 100 Gbps applies 'from day one at general availability' — a qualifier The Register's report (and consequently the article, which cites Register for this figure) omits. The article's phrasing is faithful to what The Register reported, so this is not a bot-caused misattribution, but it is a minor precision gap worth flagging since the primary source is more specific about the GA/preview distinction.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (dates, regions, quotes, the OCI-reached-GA claim, the April prior-coverage framing) check out against the source snapshots, with the one exception noted above: the 'consistent connectivity experiences across...' string presented in quotation marks as an AWS quote is a paraphrase, not a verbatim reproduction. This is a single, subordinate-claim-level issue (not in the headline, summary, or lead) that a corrections note can honestly cover.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. The Register's regulatory-irony angle (AWS/Microsoft previously downplaying multicloud friction to competition regulators) is reported as attributed fact from a cited source, not adopted as the bot's own editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: Verified this is genuinely new coverage, not a re-narration. The submission's body links to /article/2026-04/22-aws-interconnect-multicloud-goes-ga-with-google-cloud-as-launch-partner-setting-an-open-spec-that-azure-and-oci-have-agreed-to-follow, which exists at that exact path and was confirmed by reading the file. That April article covers AWS Interconnect reaching GA with Google Cloud as the sole live partner, with Azure and OCI only 'committed to join later in 2026' without a firm date — it does not cover an Azure launch. This submission covers the Aug 31 event: Azure actually joining (in preview), plus the new fact that OCI has separately reached GA since April. The 'later in 2026... without giving a firm date' framing in this submission accurately echoes the April article's own 'What We Don't Know' section, which used the identical verbatim phrase 'later in 2026.' A repo-wide grep for 'interconnect' across src/content/articles/ turned up no other article covering the Azure/AWS Aug 31 announcement. The --force-follow-up justification is legitimate: this is a genuine follow-up with new developments (Azure joining, OCI status update), not a duplicate.
concerns: The article presents 'consistent connectivity experiences across Microsoft Azure (Preview), OCI (Generally Available), and Google Cloud (Generally Available)' in quotation marks as a direct AWS quote, but the AWS News Blog's actual wording is 'a consistent, simple experience to our customers on Microsoft Azure (Preview), OCI (Generally Available), and Google Cloud (Generally Available).' The status labels are correct; the framing language around them is paraphrased, not verbatim.

The 100 Gbps figure is cited to The Register, which reported it without the 'at general availability' qualifier that Microsoft's own Azure Blog attaches to it. The article's phrasing is faithful to what Register wrote, so this is not treated as a corrections-worthy bot error, but it is noted for awareness.

editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively solid, well-sourced follow-up story with a legitimate justification for bypassing the topic-collision gate.
